sesoi.quantity: D_marginal (defects surfaced ONLY by the clean-archive wheel contract)
sesoi.definition: The smallest effect of interest is ONE genuinely-missed first-party defect: a single unpackaged-namespace import that raises ModuleNotFoundError on clean install and that no pre-existing CI gate flags on the same snapshot. Below D_marginal=1 the flagship RQ adds nothing.
sesoi.rationale: SESOI is pinned to the preregistered margin (prereg_margin=1 in benchmarks/flagship_baselines/comparison_report.json). It is a substantive, pre-committed threshold, not a post-hoc p<0.05 line.

detection_rate.definition: per-module Bernoulli detection: fraction of packaged first-party modules the clean-archive check flags as failing
detection_rate.n_note: N is an approximate census denominator: count of .py modules under the packaged top-level namespaces. It bounds the detection rate; the PRIMARY effect size is the count D, which needs no denominator.

comparator_effect.note: Every baseline catches 0 on snapshot S; the entire 70 is marginal detection.

intervals.note: Treats D as a Poisson count. Excludes the SESOI-null (D<1) by a wide margin.
Counts the 11 distinct unpackaged-import roots as the independent units (see dependence_caveat). Even the cluster-collapsed count is >> SESOI.
Resamples whole clusters with replacement; the wide interval reflects the heavy imbalance (one 'research' cluster = 41 rows). Lower bound still >> SESOI.
Exact binomial CI on p under an independent-Bernoulli-per-module assumption (violated; see dependence_caveat). Interval excludes p=0.

primary_report.statement: Effect size D_marginal = 70 (66 distinct modules, 11 independent defect roots), exact-Poisson 95% CI [54.57, 88.44]; cluster-adjusted 95% CI [5.49, 19.68]. This effect-size-plus-interval is the primary result. No bare p-value is reported.

dependence_caveat.explanation: The 70 module-level failures are NOT independent trials. They cluster on 11 distinct unpackaged-import ROOTS (research=41, runtime=13, geosync_hpc=5, instrument_validation=3, rl=2, cortex_service/tacl/envs/governance/tests/physics_contracts=1 each). A single missing top-level package fails every module that imports it simultaneously, so the effective number of independent defects is ~11, not 70.
dependence_caveat.consequence: Row-level intervals (Poisson on 70, Clopper-Pearson on 66/1517) UNDERSTATE uncertainty because they treat correlated rows as independent. The cluster-adjusted Poisson (on 11) and the cluster bootstrap are the honest-uncertainty framings and are carried as PRIMARY_cluster_adjusted / dependence_robust.

census_vs_sample.explanation: The population is finite and fully enumerated: every first-party module packaged into the wheel is scanned, not a random sample from a larger universe. For snapshot S, D_marginal = 70 is EXACT. A census carries no design-based sampling error. The Poisson / binomial / bootstrap intervals above are therefore SUPERPOPULATION / illustrative devices (answering 'if this snapshot were one draw from a hypothetical repo-generating process, what count range is consistent'), NOT sampling CIs on the census total.

power_adequacy.method: The census + every interval places the lower confidence bound far above the SESOI (min lower bound = 5.49 clusters / 16 rows >> 1). Power to detect D>=1 is effectively 1; the count analysis is NOT sampling-underpowered.
power_adequacy.note: Adequate STATISTICAL power does NOT license a binary flagship verdict: adequacy here is about the count magnitude, while the binary verdict is gated separately by reproducibility (see reproducibility_caveat).

underpowered_refusal.rule: REFUSE any binary SUPPORTED/REJECTED claim if (i) any primary interval includes the SESOI-null 'no marginal defect' (lower bound < 1), OR (ii) the census/sample is too small to resolve the SESOI, OR (iii) the same-snapshot reproducibility leg is unverified.
underpowered_refusal.decision_reason: The effect is large and well-bounded (NOT underpowered), but the RES-008 same-snapshot reproducibility leg (reproducibility_verified_at_S=false) is unmet, so the binary 'flagship proven' verdict is withheld. This matches RES-008's INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE.

reproducibility_caveat.detail: Two independent reruns at current HEAD gave a bit-identical defect set (74==74). But the committed snapshot-S artifact reports 70 defects under a different wheel_sha (stale-vs-HEAD), and no same-S rerun was executed. Prereg criterion (2) reproducibility-at-S is therefore NOT verified. Source: benchmarks/flagship_baselines/comparison_report.json.

sensitivity.assumption: dependence structure (independent rows vs clustered roots)
sensitivity.finding: Under EVERY dependence assumption the lower bound stays far above SESOI=1. The qualitative conclusion 'marginal detection >> SESOI' is INSENSITIVE to whether we count rows, distinct modules, or independent roots.

sensitivity.assumption: snapshot choice (committed S vs current HEAD)
sensitivity.finding: Both snapshot counts are >> SESOI; the marginal-detection conclusion is insensitive to snapshot choice. The 4-defect drift is a REPRODUCIBILITY/measurement issue (drives the withheld binary verdict), not a magnitude issue.
The detection rate's lower bound stays strictly above 0 across plausible N; the count-based effect size (which needs no N) is the primary result and is unaffected.

honesty_note: The effect size is real and large (D_marginal=70, tight lower bounds), but this report deliberately does NOT convert it into a binary 'flagship proven' / SUPPORTED claim. Consistent with RES-008, the same-snapshot reproducibility gap keeps the verdict at INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. This is a CENSUS (no sampling uncertainty) with a residual measurement/reproducibility caveat, not a sampling study. No p-value is the headline; the effect size and its interval are.

computation_notes.clopper_pearson: beta.ppf tails on (x, n-x+1) and (x+1, n-x)
computation_notes.cluster_bootstrap: 20000 resamples of the 11 root-clusters with replacement, seed 20260719, 2.5/97.5 percentiles
